en: Netti Paṭiniddesavāra Vibhaṅga 11: Analysis of the Section on Further Exposition of the Guide-Line (Netti) [The following is a translation of the specific section: **Analysis of the Section on Further Exposition of the Guide-Line** **1. Analysis of the Ninefold Thread** *The Ninefold Thread:* (1) **The Thread of the Teaching:** "Bhikkhus, there are these four foundations of mindfulness. (2) **The Thread of the Meaning:** "What, bhikkhus, is the noble truth of suffering? (3) **The Thread of the Language:** "Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One, directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, applicable, to be personally experienced by the wise. (4) **The Thread of the Person:** "When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is possessed of faith, he is capable of attaining the destruction of the taints. (5) **The Thread of the Abiding:** "In whatever way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells with a mind well-restrained, his mind becomes pliant. (6) **The Thread of the Mode:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three modes of conduct. (7) **The Thread of the Characteristic:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three characteristics of the conditioned. (8) **The Thread of the Synthesis:** "Bhikkhus, all that is subject to origination is subject to cessation. (9) **The Thread of the Investigation:** "Bhikkhus, what is the Noble Truth of Suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, sickness is suffering, death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are suffering; association with the disliked is suffering, separation from the liked is suffering, not getting what one desires is suffering; in short, the five aggregates of clinging are suffering. **2. Analysis of the Tenfold Thread** *The Tenfold Thread:* (1) **The Thread of the Teaching:** "Bhikkhus, there are these four establishments of mindfulness. (2) **The Thread of the Meaning:** "What, bhikkhus, is the noble truth of the origin of suffering? (3) **The Thread of the Language:** "Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One... [as above]... to be personally experienced by the wise. (4) **The Thread of the Person:** "When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is possessed of virtue, he is capable of attaining the destruction of the taints. (5) **The Thread of the Abiding:** "In whatever way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells with a mind well-concentrated, his wisdom becomes clear. (6) **The Thread of the Mode:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three modes of practice. (7) **The Thread of the Characteristic:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three characteristics of the unconditioned. (8) **The Thread of the Synthesis:** "Bhikkhus, all that is subject to arising is subject to cessation. (9) **The Thread of the Investigation:** "Bhikkhus, what is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering? It is the complete fading away and cessation of that craving, which is accompanied by delight and lust, seeking delight here and there; namely, the relinquishing, the letting go, the abandoning, and the rejecting of it. (10) **The Thread of the Analysis:** "Bhikkhus, what is the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering? It is this Noble Eightfold Path, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. **3. Analysis of the Elevenfold Thread** *The Elevenfold Thread:* (1) **The Thread of the Teaching:** "Bhikkhus, there are these four right strivings. (2) **The Thread of the Meaning:** "What, bhikkhus, is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering? (3) **The Thread of the Language:** "Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One... [as above]... to be personally experienced by the wise. (4) **The Thread of the Person:** "When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is possessed of learning, he is capable of attaining the destruction of the taints. (5) **The Thread of the Abiding:** "In whatever way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells with energy aroused, his mind becomes liberated from the taints. (6) **The Thread of the Mode:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three modes of progress. (7) **The Thread of the Characteristic:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three characteristics of the ultimate. (8) **The Thread of the Synthesis:** "Bhikkhus, all that is subject to arising is subject to cessation. (9) **The Thread of the Investigation:** "Bhikkhus, what is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering? It is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving... [as above]... the rejection of it. (10) **The Thread of the Analysis:** "Bhikkhus, what is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering? It is this Noble Eightfold Path... [as above]... right concentration. (11) **The Thread of the Comprehension:** "Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu has comprehended the Four Noble Truths, he is called one who has attained the goal. **4. Analysis of the Twelvefold Thread** *The Twelvefold Thread:* (1) **The Thread of the Teaching:** "Bhikkhus, there are these four bases of psychic power. (2) **The Thread of the Meaning:** "What, bhikkhus, is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering? (3) **The Thread of the Language:** "Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One... [as above]... to be personally experienced by the wise. (4) **The Thread of the Person:** "When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is possessed of wisdom, he is capable of attaining the destruction of the taints. (5) **The Thread of the Abiding:** "In whatever way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells with a mind well-liberated, he attains Nibbāna. (6) **The Thread of the Mode:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three modes of liberation. (7) **The Thread of the Characteristic:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three characteristics of the ultimate. (8) **The Thread of the Synthesis:** "Bhikkhus, all that is subject to arising is subject to cessation. (9) **The Thread of the Investigation:** "Bhikkhus, what is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering? It is the remainderless fading away and cessation of that same craving... [as above]... the rejection of it. (10) **The Thread of the Analysis:** "Bhikkhus, what is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering? It is this Noble Eightfold Path... [as above]... right concentration. (11) **The Thread of the Comprehension:** "Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu has comprehended the Four Noble Truths, he is called one who has attained the goal. (12) **The Thread of the Realization:** "Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu has realized the Four Noble Truths, he is called one who has reached the end of the journey. **5. Analysis of the Thirteenfold Thread** *The Thirteenfold Thread:* (1) **The Thread of the Teaching:** "Bhikkhus, there are these four fruits of the ascetic life. (2) **The Thread of the Meaning:** "What, bhikkhus, is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering? (3) **The Thread of the Language:** "Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is well-expounded by the Blessed One... [as above]... to be personally experienced by the wise. (4) **The Thread of the Person:** "When, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is possessed of faith, he is capable of attaining the fruit of stream-entry. (5) **The Thread of the Abiding:** "In whatever way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells with a mind well-restrained, he attains the first jhāna. (6) **The Thread of the Mode:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three modes of attainment. (7) **The Thread of the Characteristic:** "Bhikkhus, there are these three characteristics of the conditioned. (8) **The Thread of the Synthesis:** "Bhikkhus, all that is subject to origination is subject to cessation. (9) **The Thread of the Investigation:**
The Analysis of the Mode of Conveying Descriptions.
Therein, what is the mode of conveying descriptions?
“The Blessed One teaches one Dhamma by means of various descriptions.”
That which is a teaching by way of a basic exposition is a "description by way of presentation" (*nikkhepapaññatti*).
And what is a teaching by way of a basic exposition? It is the Four Noble Truths.
As the Blessed One said:
“This is suffering”—this designation is a designation of relinquishment for the five aggregates, the six elements, the eighteen elements, the twelve bases, and the ten faculties.
For if, monks, there is lust for physical nutriment, if there is delight, if there is craving, consciousness becomes established there and grows.
Wherever consciousness is established and grows, there is the descent of name-and-form.
Where there is the descent of name-and-form, there is the growth of volitional formations.
Where there is the growth of volitional formations, there is the production of renewed existence in the future.
Where there is the production of renewed existence in the future, there is birth, aging, and death in the future.
Where there is birth, aging, and death in the future, I say, monks, that it is accompanied by sorrow, accompanied by fear, and accompanied by despair.
This is also true regarding contact... [and so on].
If, monks, there is lust for the nutriment of mental volition,
if there is delight, if there is craving for the nutriment of consciousness, then consciousness becomes established there and grows.
Wherever consciousness becomes established and grows, there is the descent of name-and-form.
Where there is the descent of name-and-form, there is the growth of volitional formations.
Where there is the growth of volitional formations, there is the production of renewed existence in the future.
Where there is the production of renewed existence in the future, there is birth, aging, and death in the future.
"Wherever there is future birth, aging, and death, that, monks, I call 'with sorrow,' 'with fear,' and 'with despair.
This is the description of the origin of suffering and its arising.
If, monks, there is no lust for physical food, no delight, and no craving, then consciousness does not become established there and does not grow."
Where consciousness is unestablished and does not grow, there is no descent of name-and-form.
Where there is no descent of name-and-form, there is no growth of volitional formations.
Where there is no growth of volitional formations, there is no production of renewed existence in the future.
Where there is no production of renewed existence in the future, there is no birth, aging, and death in the future.
Where there is no birth, aging, and death in the future, I say, monks, that it is sorrowless, free from distress, and without despair. This is also true regarding contact... [and so on].
If, monks, there is no lust, no delight, and no craving for the nutriment of mental volition;
and if, monks, there is no lust, no delight, and no craving for the nutriment of consciousness, then consciousness does not become established there and does not grow.
Where consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no descent of name-and-form.
Where there is no descent of name-and-form, there is no growth of volitional formations.
Where there is no growth of volitional formations, there is no production of renewed existence in the future.
Where there is no production of renewed existence in the future, there is no birth, aging, and death in the future.
"Where there is no future birth, aging, and death—that, monks, I call sorrowless, dustless, and free from despair.

This is the designation of full understanding for suffering, the designation of abandoning for its origin, the designation of development for the path, and the designation of realization for cessation.
Monks, develop concentration."
"Monks, a monk who is diligent, discerning, mindful, and concentrated understands things as they truly are.
And what does he understand as it truly is?
He understands, 'The eye is impermanent,' as it truly is."
“He understands as it really is: ‘Forms are impermanent. He understands as it really is: ‘Eye-consciousness is impermanent.
He understands as it really is: ‘Eye-contact is impermanent.
And he understands as it really is that whatever feeling arises conditioned by eye-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is impermanent.”
The ear … the nose … the tongue … [the body] … the mind.
He understands as it really is: "The body... the mind is impermanent.
He understands as it really is: "Mental phenomena are impermanent."
“He understands, as it truly is, that ‘mind-consciousness is impermanent.
He understands, as it truly is, that ‘mind-contact is impermanent.
And he understands, as it truly is, that whatever feeling arises conditioned by mind-contact—whether pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is impermanent.”

This is the designation of development for the path, the designation of full understanding for suffering, the designation of abandoning for the origin, and the designation of realization for cessation.
Scatter form, Rādha, blow it away, destroy it, make it incapable of being played with; practice with wisdom for the destruction of craving.
With the destruction of craving comes the destruction of suffering; with the destruction of suffering comes Nibbāna.
Disperse feeling...
perception...
volitional formations... consciousness; shatter it, demolish it, make it a thing of play, and proceed with wisdom toward the destruction of craving.
With the destruction of craving comes the destruction of suffering; with the destruction of suffering comes Nibbāna.

This is the description of cessation for cessation, the description of disenchantment for gratification, the description of full understanding for suffering, the description of abandoning for its origin, the description of development for the path, and the description of realization for cessation.
One understands, as it truly is, "This is suffering," and one understands, as it truly is, "This is the origin of suffering."
“He understands as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering’; he understands as it really is: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.

This is the designation of penetration regarding the truths, the designation of presentation regarding the plane of seeing, the designation of development regarding the path, and the designation of realization regarding the fruit of stream-entry.”
He understands as it really is: “These are the taints”; he understands as it really is: “This is the origin of the taints”; he understands as it really is: “This is the cessation of the taints”;
he understands as it really is: “This is the way leading to the cessation of the taints”;
he understands as it really is: “These taints cease without remainder.”
This is a description of arising for the knowledge of destruction; a description of opportunity for the knowledge of non-arising;
a description of development for the path; a description of full understanding for suffering; a description of abandoning for the origin;
a description of exertion for the faculty of energy; a description of removal for the gadflies; a description of laying down for the plane of development; a description of striking down...
“Of evil, unwholesome states.
Monks, regarding these things unheard of before, there arose in me the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true insight, and light, that “this is suffering.
Monks, regarding this as “the origin of suffering,” there arose in me... [and so on].
“This is the cessation of suffering,” monks, ...
“This is the practice leading to the cessation of suffering”—thus, monks, regarding these things unheard of before, there arose in me vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.

This is the designation of the teachings as the Truths; it is the designation of their presentation through wisdom consisting of what has been heard; it is the designation of their realization through the faculty of “I shall come to know the unknown”; it is the designation of the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma.
“‘This suffering, indeed, is to be fully understood’— thus, monks, regarding things unheard of before, there arose in me the eye, knowledge, wisdom, true insight, and light.
‘This origin of suffering, indeed, is to be abandoned’— thus,
monks …pe… ‘This cessation of suffering, indeed, is to be realized’— thus, monks …pe…”

“Moreover, ‘this practice leading to the cessation of suffering is to be developed’—monks, regarding these states unheard of before, there arose in me vision, knowledge, wisdom, true insight, and light.

This is the designation of development for the path; it is the designation of relinquishment for wisdom consisting of reflection; it is the designation of realization for the faculty of final knowledge.”
“‘This suffering has been fully understood’—this, monks, regarding things unheard of before, there arose in me vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.
‘This origin of suffering has been abandoned’—this, monks, ...
‘This cessation of suffering has been realized’—this, monks, ...”

“Furthermore, ‘this practice leading to the cessation of suffering has been developed’—monks, regarding these things unheard of before, there arose in me vision, knowledge, wisdom, true knowledge, and light.

This is the designation by way of development for the path; the designation by way of relinquishment for the wisdom consisting in development; the designation by way of realization for the faculty of one who has known; and the designation by way of turning for the Wheel of Dhamma.
“The measurable and the immeasurable, and their origin,”
The Sage relinquished the formative force of existence;
delighting in the internal and composed,
he shattered his own rebirth like a coat of mail.
“Measurable” refers to the element of formations (*saṅkhāradhātu*).
“Unmeasurable” refers to the element of Nibbāna. “Both the measurable and the unmeasurable arising” is a designation for all phenomena by way of direct knowledge (*abhiññā*).
It is a designation by way of relinquishment (*nikkhepa*) for the analytical knowledge of phenomena (*dhammapaṭisambhidā*).
“‘The sage abandoned the formative activity of existence’—this is a designation for the origin [of suffering] by way of relinquishment.
‘[He is] one who has fully understood’—this is a designation for suffering.
‘Delighting inwardly, composed’—this is a designation for development by way of mindfulness directed to the body.”
“Establishment” is a designation for one-pointedness of mind.

“He shattered the self-origination like a coat of mail” is a designation for the mind’s emergence from existence; “clinging” is a designation for omniscience; “crushing” is a designation for the eggshell of ignorance.
Therefore the Blessed One said: “The measurable and the immeasurable origination.”
“How could a person who has seen suffering and its source bow down to sensual pleasures?
For having understood that in the world sensual pleasures are a snare, [one should abandon them].”
“Let one who possesses mindfulness train for their discipline.
The phrase “that which is suffering” is both a designation by synonym and a designation by full understanding of suffering.
The phrase “from whatever source it arises” is both a designation of origin and a designation of the abandoning of that origin.
“‘He has seen’” is both a designation by synonym for the eye of knowledge and a designation for its penetration.
“‘How could that person incline toward sensual pleasures? is both a designation by synonym and a designation for the adherence to craving for sensual pleasures.
“‘Having known that sensual pleasures are a fetter in the world’” is a designation for viewing sensual pleasures as enemies.
For sensual pleasures are like embers, like pieces of meat, like fire, and like a pit of snakes.

“The mindful one among them” is a designation for diminution in the sense of abandoning; it is a designation for relinquishment in the sense of mindfulness directed to the body; it is a designation for development in the sense of the Path.
“One should train for their removal” is a designation for penetration in the sense of the removal of lust, the removal of hatred, and the removal of delusion.
“Beings” is a designation of synonyms for the practitioner.

For when the practitioner understands that sensual pleasures are a fetter, he generates wholesome states for the non-arising of sensual pleasures; he exerts himself for the arising of wholesome states that have not yet arisen.
This is the description of effort for the attainment of what has not yet been attained.
This is the description of relinquishment regarding dissatisfaction with what is merely trifling.
In this context, when one exerts effort for the stability of wholesome states that have arisen, this is the description of diligence (*appamāda*).
It is a designation for development; it is a designation for the relinquishing of the faculty of energy; it is a designation for the protection of wholesome states;
it is a designation for the stability of the training in higher consciousness.
Therefore the Blessed One said: “He who has seen suffering and its source...”
“The world is bound by delusion,
yet it appears as if it were real;
the fool is bound by acquisitions.”
Enveloped by darkness,
it appears like a mirage;
for one who looks at it, there is nothing at all.
“‘The world is bound by delusion’: this is a teaching-designation (*desanā-paññatti*) for the perversions (*vipallāsa*).
‘He appears as one capable [of liberation]’: this is a designation of perversion (*viparīta-paññatti*) regarding the world.

‘The fool is bound by acquisitions (*upadhi*)’: this is a designation of origin (*pabhava-paññatti*) for the sphere of evil desires, and a designation of function (*kicca-paññatti*) for the obsessions (*pariyuṭṭhāna*).”
The designation of strength refers to the defilements.
The designation of growth refers to formations.
“Enveloped in darkness” is a designation of teaching and a synonymic designation for the darkness of ignorance.
“‘She appears like a woman’” is a designation of seeing pertaining to the divine eye; “‘When seen, there is nothing at all’” is a designation of relinquishment pertaining to the eye of wisdom.
“‘For one who sees, there is nothing at all’” is a designation of penetration regarding beings: lust is a possession, hatred is a possession, and delusion is a possession.
Therefore the Blessed One said, “The world is bound by delusion.”

“There is, monks, an unborn, unbecome, unmade, and unconditioned. If, monks, there were not this unborn, unbecome, unmade, and unconditioned, an escape from the born, become, made, and conditioned would not be discerned here.
But because there is, monks, an unborn, unbecome, unmade, and unconditioned, therefore an escape from the born, become, made, and conditioned is discerned.”
“If, monks, this unborn, unbecome, unmade, and unconditioned were not,” this is a declaration of teaching and a declaration of synonyms for Nibbāna.
“For there would be no escape discerned here from the born, the become, the made, and the conditioned,” this is a declaration of synonyms and a declaration of the leading away from the conditioned.
“But because, monks, there is an unborn, an unbecome, an unmade, and an unconditioned,” this is a declaration of synonyms and a declaration that illuminates Nibbāna.

“Therefore, an escape from what is born, become, made, and conditioned is discerned”—this is a designation by synonyms for Nibbāna, a designation as leading out for the Path, and a designation as escape from saṃsāra.
Thus the Blessed One said: “If this, bhikkhus, were not to exist.
And thus the Venerable Mahākaccāyana said: “The Blessed One teaches one Dhamma by means of various designations.”
The Mode of Conveying Description is concluded.
